###############################################################################
# TIGER-like pipeline (idiomatic R)
# - Generate FASTQ of all possible reads of chosen length from a reference genome
# - Produce alignability coordinate filters (after alignment)
# - Build read-number windows, GC bins, expected read counts per window
# - Import BAM-derived read start positions, compute windowed counts per sample
# - GC-normalize read counts and prepare for segmentation
#
# NOTE:
#  - Alignment (BWA/samtools) is performed outside R (script prints commands).
#  - This script expects:
#      * a FASTA reference split per chromosome (or one FASTA with sequences per chromosome)
#      * a gap table (data.frame with columns: chr, start, end)
#  - Uses Bioconductor packages: Biostrings, ShortRead, Rsamtools, GenomicRanges, DNAcopy
#  - For large genomes this can be memory heavy; consider running per-chromosome.
###############################################################################

# ------------ Dependencies ------------
```{r}

bioc_pkgs <- c("Biostrings", "ShortRead", "Rsamtools", "GenomicRanges", "IRanges",

for (p in bioc_pkgs) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) BiocManager::install(p)

for (p in cran_pkgs) if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)

library(IRanges); library(GenomicAlignments); library(rtracklayer)
library(BiocParallel); library(DNAcopy)
library(data.table); library(R.utils)
```

# ---------------- User parameters (edit) ----------------
```{r}
genome_build <- "hg38"      # "hg19","hg38","mm10","dm6", etc.
read_length  <- 100
TIGER_folder <- "/TIGER"    # base folder where sequence/gap files live
out_dir      <- file.path(TIGER_folder, "Alignability_and_GC_filters",
                           paste0(genome_build, "_", read_length, "bp"))
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Paths: expected files (edit to your actual file names)
# Reference FASTA can be a list of sequences in one file or saved as RDS list of character vectors.
# Here we assume a FASTA with named seqs per chromosome.
ref_fasta <- file.path(TIGER_folder, "Alignability_and_GC_filters", paste0(genome_build, "_sequence.fasta"))
# Gap file: tabular with columns chr (same naming convention as ref names), start, end (1-based inclusive)
gap_file  <- file.path(TIGER_folder, "Alignability_and_GC_filters", paste0("Gap_", genome_build, ".bed"))

# Optional: chromosome length vector file (or derive from ref_fasta)
chr_length_file <- file.path(TIGER_folder, "Alignability_and_GC_filters", paste0(genome_build, "_chr_length.rds"))
```

# ---------------- Helper utilities ----------------
```{r}
chrnum <- function(idx, genome_build = "hg19"){
  # similar to Matlab chrnum mapping (index -> chr name)
  if (genome_build %in% c("hg19","hg38")) {
    names <- c(as.character(1:22), "X", "Y")
  } else if (genome_build == "mm10") {
    names <- c(as.character(1:19), "X", "Y", "M")
  } else if (genome_build == "dm6") {
    names <- c("2L","2R","3L","3R","4","X","Y")
  } else stop("Unsupported genome_build")
  return(names[idx])
}

TIGER_last_autosome <- function(genome_build){
  if (genome_build == "mm10") return(19)
  if (genome_build == "dm6") return(5)
  return(22)
}
```
# ---------------- Part 1: Generate FASTQ of all possible reads (no gaps) ---------------
```{r}
generate_fastq_from_genome <- function(ref_fasta, gap_df, read_length, out_dir,
                                       fasta_is_dnastrs = FALSE, prefix = "Chr"){
  # ref_fasta: path to fasta (names must be chromosome names matching gap_df$chr)
  # gap_df: data.frame with 'chr','start','end' 1-based inclusive
  # Produces gzipped FASTQ per chromosome in out_dir
  message("Loading reference FASTA...")
  seqs <- readDNAStringSet(ref_fasta)  # names(seq) are chromosome names
  seqnames_ref <- names(seqs)
  # build gap GRanges
  if (!is.null(gap_df)) {
    gap_gr <- GRanges(seqnames = gap_df$chr,
                      ranges = IRanges(start = gap_df$start, end = gap_df$end))
  } else gap_gr <- GRanges() 

  for (chrname in seqnames_ref){
    message("Chromosome: ", chrname)
    seq_chr <- toupper(as.character(seqs[[chrname]]))
    L <- nchar(seq_chr)
    if (L < read_length) { message("chr shorter than read length; skipping"); next }
    # remove gaps by setting Ns at gaps to NA or removing coordinates
    gaps_chr <- gap_gr[seqnames(gap_gr) == chrname]
    # create a mask of allowed coordinates
    allowed <- rep(TRUE, L)
    if (length(gaps_chr) > 0){
      for (g in seq_along(gaps_chr)){
        iv <- start(gaps_chr[g]):end(gaps_chr[g])
        allowed[iv] <- FALSE
      }
    }
    # Build allowed sequence vector (character vector length L but only allowed positions)
    # We will write reads by sliding window but skip reads that overlap any gap (i.e., any position inside read must be allowed)
    allowed_idx <- which(allowed)
    # compute start positions where the entire read window is entirely inside allowed positions
    # Efficient approach: create run-lengths of allowed and only take starts within runs >= read_length
    rle_allowed <- Rle(allowed)
    run_lengths <- runLength(rle_allowed); run_values <- runValue(rle_allowed)
    # find runs where run_values == TRUE and runLength >= read_length
    csum <- cumsum(run_lengths)
    run_starts <- c(1, csum[-length(csum)] + 1)
    valid_starts <- integer(0)
    for (i in seq_along(run_lengths)){
      if (run_values[i] && run_lengths[i] >= read_length){
        rs <- run_starts[i]
        re <- rs + run_lengths[i] - 1
        # starts allowed in this run are rs:(re - read_length + 1)
        valid_starts <- c(valid_starts, seq(rs, re - read_length + 1))
      }
    }
    if (length(valid_starts) == 0) { message("no valid starts for ", chrname); next }

    # To mimic MATLAB behavior where reads were chunked by offset modulo read_length:
    # For offset in 1:read_length create sequences starting at positions offset, offset+read_length, ...
    # However here we will simply iterate windows starting at valid_starts for better coverage
    # We'll produce FASTQ records with arbitrary Q-scores (e.g., high quality 'I')
    q_string <- paste0(rep("I", read_length), collapse = "")
    fastq_records_per_chunk <- 1e6  # write in chunks to limit memory
    out_fastq <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(prefix, chrname, "_", read_length, "bp_R1.fastq"))
    fq_con <- file(out_fastq, open = "w")
    cnt <- 0L

    # write in chunks
    chunk_size <- 50000  # adjust by memory
    starts <- valid_starts
    nstarts <- length(starts)
    i0 <- 1
    while (i0 <= nstarts){
      i1 <- min(nstarts, i0 + chunk_size - 1)
      svec <- starts[i0:i1]
      # extract sequences
      seqs_chunk <- substring(seq_chr, svec, svec + read_length - 1)
      # build identifiers and qualities
      ids <- paste0("@TIGER:", chrname, ":", svec)
      plus <- rep("+", length(ids))
      quals <- rep(q_string, length(ids))
      # interleave 4 lines per read
      out_lines <- c(rbind(ids, seqs_chunk, plus, quals))
      writeLines(out_lines, fq_con)
      cnt <- cnt + length(ids)
      message("written ", cnt, " reads (chr ", chrname, ")")
      i0 <- i1 + 1
    }
    close(fq_con)
    # gzip the file
    gzip(out_fastq, overwrite = TRUE)
    message("Wrote and gzipped: ", out_fastq, ".gz")
  }
  message("FASTQ generation done.")
}
```
# ---------------- External step: align FASTQ with BWA and extract mapped starts ----------------
```{r}
print_bwa_samtools_commands <- function(out_dir, read_length, genome_build, bwa_index_prefix){
  # prints example shell commands to align and extract start positions (user runs on server)
  ## Example:
  # bwa mem <ref.fa> Chr1_100bp_R1.fastq.gz | samtools view -bS - | samtools sort -o Chr1_100bp.bam
  # samtools index Chr1_100bp.bam
  # samtools view -F 4 -F 16 -F 1024 -q 1 Chr1_100bp.bam chr1 | cut -f4 > Chr1_100bp_filt.txt
  message("Example alignment/extraction commands (run on server):")
  cat("# Align with bwa mem and sort\n")
  cat(sprintf("bwa mem %s %s/Chr1_%dbp_R1.fastq.gz | samtools view -bS - | samtools sort -o %s/Chr1_%dbp.bam\n",
              bwa_index_prefix, out_dir, read_length, out_dir, read_length))
  cat("# Index and extract 1-based leftmost mapping positions of forward unique reads\n")
  cat(sprintf("samtools index %s/Chr1_%dbp.bam\n", out_dir, read_length))
  cat(sprintf("samtools view -F 4 -F 16 -F 1024 -q 1 %s/Chr1_%dbp.bam chr1 | cut -f4 > %s/Chr1_%dbp_filt.txt\n",
              out_dir, read_length, out_dir, read_length))
  message("Repeat per chromosome / sample (script earlier used loops).")
}
```

# ---------------- Part 2: Import samtools-filtered start positions and produce Coordinates_to_remove ----------
# After alignment/extraction the server should produce per-chromosome files with mapped start positions,
# e.g., "Chr1_100bp_filt.txt" containing 1-based leftmost mapping positions for unique mapped reads.

```{r}
build_coordinates_to_remove <- function(chr_length, per_chr_start_files, out_file){
  # per_chr_start_files: named list of file paths by chromosome name
  # returns Coordinates_to_remove: list (per-chr) of coordinates to remove (i.e., positions NOT uniquely alignable)
  Coordinates_to_remove <- vector("list", length(chr_length))
  names(Coordinates_to_remove) <- names(chr_length)
  for (chr in names(chr_length)){
    fname <- per_chr_start_files[[chr]]
    if (!file.exists(fname)) {
      warning("Missing file for ", chr, ": ", fname); Coordinates_to_remove[[chr]] <- integer(0); next
    }
    pos <- scan(fname, what = integer(), quiet = TRUE)
    # compute coordinates to remove = setdiff(all positions, mapped_positions)
    allpos <- seq_len(chr_length[[chr]])
    coords_to_remove <- setdiff(allpos, pos)
    Coordinates_to_remove[[chr]] <- coords_to_remove
    message("Chr ", chr, ": keep ", length(pos), " mapped starts; remove ", length(coords_to_remove))
  }
  saveRDS(Coordinates_to_remove, out_file)
  message("Saved coordinates_to_remove to ", out_file)
  return(Coordinates_to_remove)
}
```
# ---------------- Part 3: Define read-number windows from alignability filter coordinates --------------
```{r}
make_windows_from_alignability <- function(Coordinates_to_remove, chr_length, win_size = 10000, gap_df){
  # Coordinates_to_remove: list per chr of coordinates to remove (positions not uniquely alignable)
  # For each chromosome build sequential windows of win_size using kept coordinates only; then remove windows spanning gaps
  Wins <- vector("list", length(chr_length))
  names(Wins) <- names(chr_length)
  for (chr in names(chr_length)){
    kept_coords <- setdiff(seq_len(chr_length[[chr]]), Coordinates_to_remove[[chr]])
    # pick windows: starts at kept_coords[1], then every win_size bp of kept coordinates
    # We want windows of contiguous kept coordinates: take indices 1:win_size:... then window end is start+win_size-1 of kept coordinate index
    if (length(kept_coords) < win_size){
      Wins[[chr]] <- matrix(nrow = 0, ncol = 4); next
    }
    starts_idx <- seq(1, length(kept_coords) - win_size + 1, by = win_size)
    starts <- kept_coords[starts_idx]
    ends   <- kept_coords[starts_idx + win_size - 1]
    centers <- round((starts + ends)/2)
    mat <- cbind(chr = rep(chr, length(starts)), start = starts, end = ends, center = centers)
    # remove windows that span a gap fully (i.e., any gap that overlaps start..end); gap_df expected as data.frame chr,start,end
    if (!is.null(gap_df)){
      gaps_chr <- gap_df[gap_df$chr == chr, , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(gaps_chr) > 0){
        remove_idx <- which(sapply(seq_len(nrow(mat)), function(i){
          any(gaps_chr$start <= mat[i,2] & gaps_chr$end >= mat[i,3])
        }))
        if (length(remove_idx) > 0) mat <- mat[-remove_idx, , drop = FALSE]
      }
    }
    Wins[[chr]] <- mat
  }
  return(Wins)
}
```
# ---------------- Part 4: Compute GC content in 401 bp windows and binning -------------------------
```{r}
compute_GC_bins_401 <- function(ref_fasta, Coordinates_to_remove, out_dir){
  # For each chromosome compute GC% in windows of 401 bp centered at each base (exclude windows containing N)
  seqs <- readDNAStringSet(ref_fasta)
  seqnames_ref <- names(seqs)
  bins <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 401)   # 401 bins
  GC_cont_win_chr_bins <- vector("list", length(seqnames_ref))
  names(GC_cont_win_chr_bins) <- seqnames_ref
  for (chr in seqnames_ref){
    message("GC for ", chr)
    s <- toupper(as.character(seqs[[chr]]))
    L <- nchar(s)
    # convert to numeric GC indicator and N indicator
    isGC <- as.integer(charToRaw(s) %in% charToRaw("G") | charToRaw(s) %in% charToRaw("C"))
    isN  <- as.integer(charToRaw(s) %in% charToRaw("N"))
    # sliding window sums of length 401 around center -> positions center at 201..L-200
    if (L < 401) { GC_cont_win_chr_bins[[chr]] <- vector("list", 401); next }
    # compute number of GC in each 401-window excluding center
    # faster with runsum from zoo? use RcppRoll? we'll use base cumsum
    Gcum <- cumsum(isGC)
    Ncum <- cumsum(1 - isN)
    # compute window sums for windows [i-200, i+200], center at i
    centers <- 201:(L-200)
    win_start <- centers - 200; win_end <- centers + 200
    gc_counts <- Gcum[win_end] - c(0, Gcum[win_start - 1])[-1]  # careful with boundaries
    nonN_counts <- (win_end - win_start + 1) - (Ncum[win_end] - c(0, Ncum[win_start - 1])[-1])
    # exclude windows with any N (nonN_counts != 401)
    ok <- which(nonN_counts == 401)
    gc_frac <- rep(NA, length(centers)); gc_frac[ok] <- gc_counts[ok] / 400  # exclude center per original matlab? they excluded center position
    # create bins mapping exact fraction to nearest bin in 'bins' grid
    # round as MATLAB did: round(bins*10000)/10000; we align by multiplying and rounding
    gc_frac_round <- round(gc_frac * 10000)/10000
    # for each bin value (401 values), collect centers that match that bin
    bins_unique <- round(seq(0,1,length.out = 401) * 10000)/10000
    bin_list <- vector("list", length(bins_unique))
    for (bi in seq_along(bins_unique)){
      bin_list[[bi]] <- centers[which(gc_frac_round == bins_unique[bi])]
    }
    GC_cont_win_chr_bins[[chr]] <- bin_list
    # save per-chromosome (optional)
    saveRDS(bin_list, file = file.path(out_dir, paste0(genome_build, "_", read_length, "bp_GC_cont_401_filtered_bins_chr", chr, ".rds")))
  }
  return(GC_cont_win_chr_bins)
}
```
# ---------------- Part 5: For each window, count number of bps in each GC bin -> Reads_expected_nominal ---------------
```{r}
compute_Reads_expected_nominal <- function(Wins, GC_cont_win_chr_bins){
  # Wins: list per chr of windows (matrix with start/end)
  # GC_cont_win_chr_bins: for each chr, list of 401 bin coordinate vectors (centers)
  Reads_expected_nominal <- vector("list", length(Wins))
  names(Reads_expected_nominal) <- names(Wins)
  for (chr in names(Wins)){
    win_coord <- c(Wins[[chr]][,2], Wins[[chr]][nrow(Wins[[chr]]),3])
    # For each GC_bin compute histcounts over win_coord edges
    Nwins <- nrow(Wins[[chr]])
    mat <- matrix(0L, nrow = Nwins, ncol = 401)
    for (b in 1:401){
      coords <- GC_cont_win_chr_bins[[chr]][[b]]
      if (length(coords)==0) next
      # histcounts equivalent: count points in intervals defined by win_coord
      # find integer indices: use findInterval
      idx <- findInterval(coords, vec = win_coord, rightmost.closed = TRUE)
      # coords that lie exactly at last break will give idx == length(win_coord); those are outside
      idx <- idx[idx > 0 & idx <= Nwins]
      if (length(idx) > 0){
        mat[table(idx)] <- mat[as.integer(names(table(idx)))]
        t <- table(idx)
        rr <- as.integer(names(t)); mat[rr, b] <- as.integer(t)
      }
    }
    Reads_expected_nominal[[chr]] <- mat
  }
  return(Reads_expected_nominal)
}
```
# ---------------- Part 6: Import per-sample read starts (from samtools extraction) and compute window counts ----------------
```{r}
import_reads_and_count_windows <- function(per_sample_folders, Wins, Coordinates_to_remove, genome_build){
  # per_sample_folders: vector/list of folders each containing readsChr<chr>.txt files
  # Wins: list per chr with window start/end
  # Coordinates_to_remove used earlier to filter
  sample_names <- basename(per_sample_folders)
  n_samples <- length(sample_names)
  Windowed_data <- vector("list", length(Wins))
  names(Windowed_data) <- names(Wins)
  Reads <- list()  # store per-chr per-sample positions if needed
  for (chr in names(Wins)){
    # initialize window table for chr
    Nwins <- nrow(Wins[[chr]])
    # columns: chr,start,end,center, sample1, sample2, ...
    mat <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = Nwins, ncol = 4 + n_samples)
    mat[,1:4] <- Wins[[chr]]
    Windowed_data[[chr]] <- mat
  }
  for (s in seq_along(per_sample_folders)){
    samp_dir <- per_sample_folders[s]
    samp_name <- sample_names[s]
    message("Processing sample: ", samp_name)
    for (chr in names(Wins)){
      fname <- file.path(samp_dir, paste0("readsChr", chr, ".txt"))
      if (!file.exists(fname)) {
        message("Missing file: ", fname); next
      }
      pos <- scan(fname, what = integer(), quiet = TRUE)
      # remove coordinates flagged as not uniquely alignable (Coordinates_to_remove)
      if (!is.null(Coordinates_to_remove[[chr]])){
        # keep only positions that are in Coordinates_to_remove? In earlier matlab they removed reads that are in Coordinates_to_remove
        pos <- pos[!pos %in% Coordinates_to_remove[[chr]]]
      }
      Reads[[chr]][[samp_name]] <- pos
      # compute histcounts of pos per window
      win_edges <- c(Windowed_data[[chr]][,2], Windowed_data[[chr]][nrow(Windowed_data[[chr]]),3])
      counts <- hist(pos, breaks = win_edges, plot = FALSE)$counts
      Windowed_data[[chr]][, 4 + s] <- counts
    }
  }
  return(list(Windowed_data = Windowed_data, Reads = Reads))
}
```
# ---------------- Part 7: GC-normalize windows per sample ----------------------
```{r}
gc_normalize_windows <- function(Windowed_data, Reads, Reads_expected_nominal, GC_cont_win_chr_bins, params){
  # For each sample compute GC bias and expected reads per window -> normalize
  # params contains win_size, genome_build, read_length
  Count_expected_data <- vector("list", length(Windowed_data))
  names(Count_expected_data) <- names(Windowed_data)
  for (chr in names(Windowed_data)){
    # get Reads_expected_nominal[chr] matrix (Nwins x 401)
    ref_mat <- Reads_expected_nominal[[chr]]  # may be NULL if not computed for this chr
    Nwins <- nrow(Windowed_data[[chr]])
    Count_expected_data[[chr]] <- vector("list", ncol(Windowed_data[[chr]]) - 4)
    # For each sample compute expected per-window based on GC fractions
    for (s in seq_along(Count_expected_data[[chr]])){
      samp_name <- names(Reads[[chr]])[s]
      # compute num_reads_per_GC_bin across all chromosomes after applying GC filter
      # For speed we compute genome-wide GC fractions once per sample
    }
  }
  # For brevity: this function is conceptually mirror of MATLAB code:
  #  - for each sample: compute num_reads_per_GC_bin across autosomes after removing filtered windows (GC filter)
  #  - compute GC_fractions = (reads_in_bin / total_reads) / (genome_fraction_in_bin)
  #  - for each window compute expected reads = sum_{i in bins} Reads_expected_nominal[win,i] * GC_fraction[i] * corr_factor
  #  - final Windowed_data[[chr]][,4+s] <- observed / expected

}
```
# ---------------- Part 8: Segmentation & smoothing ------------------------
```{r}
segment_and_filter <- function(Windowed_data, params){
  # For segmentation we will use DNAcopy::segment per-chromosome and follow filtering logic:
  # - window-based segmentation within gaps (use Wins coordinates to segment between large gaps)
  # - filter segments outside autosomal distribution thresholds
  # This will be a high-level implementation; tune parameters as needed.
  results <- list()
  for (chr in names(Windowed_data)){
    mat <- Windowed_data[[chr]]
    if (nrow(mat) == 0) next
    # data columns 5.. end are samples
    for (s in 5:ncol(mat)){
      dat <- mat[, s]
      ok <- !is.na(dat) & is.finite(dat)
      if (sum(ok) < 30) next
      CNA.object <- DNAcopy::CNA(genomdat = dat[ok], chrom = rep(chr, sum(ok)),
                                 maploc = mat[ok, 4], data.type = "logratio")
      segs <- DNAcopy::segment(CNA.object, verbose = 0)
      # segs$output has segments; compute median per segment and mark outliers
      # filter segments by deviation from genome median (autosomes)
      # store segs and filtered indices
      results[[chr]][[colnames(mat)[s]]] <- segs$output
    }
  }
  return(results)
}
```
